findings.issue: 米 meaning rice (the food) is read こめ in この米, not べい (べい is the on-reading used only in compounds like 米国). The item's own expl_en even states "read こめ". Romaji 'konobei...' inherits the same error.
findings.current: このべいわとてもおいしいです
findings.suggested: このこめわとてもおいしいです

findings.issue: Token 米 has reading べい; as a standalone noun meaning rice it is read こめ. Contradicts the sentence's own explanation, which says 米 is read こめ.
中ぐらい meaning 'medium(-sized)' is read ちゅうぐらい (中位/中くらい); なかぐらい is not the standard reading in this 'medium size' sense. Romaji 'nakagurai...' inherits the error.
findings.current: なかぐらいのさいずをください
findings.suggested: ちゅうぐらいのさいずをください

findings.issue: Token 中 in 中ぐらい ('medium') is read ちゅう, not なか, in this fixed expression (中くらい/中ぐらい = ちゅうくらい/ちゅうぐらい).

The note calls まし the 'past form of ます'. Wrong: まし is the continuative stem (連用形) of ます; the past is formed by adding た (ました). As written it contradicts the next token, where た is correctly labeled the past marker. Same error in the en note.
findings.current: forma passada まし de ます
findings.suggested: forma conectiva (連用形) まし de ます, à qual se anexa o auxiliar た

findings.issue: 'conetiva' is European-Portuguese (post-agreement pt-PT) spelling; pt-BR keeps the c: 'conectiva'. Project rule mandates pt-BR.
findings.current: raiz conetiva なり (forma ます) de なる
findings.suggested: raiz conectiva なり (forma ます) de なる

findings.issue: 'o rosto de ela' is ungrammatical in Portuguese — de + ela must contract to 'dela'. The en counterpart is simply 'her face', so this is not a deliberate morpheme-by-morpheme device.
findings.current: 彼女の顔 é o sujeito (literalmente 'o rosto de ela'), marcado por が.
findings.suggested: 彼女の顔 é o sujeito (literalmente 'o rosto dela'), marcado por が.

findings.issue: lit_en glosses 台 as 'desk', which is 机, not 台 (stand/platform/table). Inconsistent with en ('table') and the token gloss ('table, counter, stand').
findings.current: As for this desk, it's very sturdy.
findings.suggested: As for this table, it's very sturdy.

findings.issue: この is proximal and only means 'this' in English; 'that' is その/あの. (pt 'este, esse' is fine for BR usage, but the en gloss is wrong; expl_en's "('this/that')" has the same problem.)

'the target te-de' leaks an internal grammar-point slug into learner-facing text; opaque to a beginner. Same leak in expl_pt ('o alvo te-de'). Should name the pattern readably, e.g. the 〜て/〜で linking form.
findings.current: This is precisely the target te-de: using 〜て to join qualities
findings.suggested: This is precisely the target 〜て/〜で linking pattern: using 〜て to join qualities

findings.issue: lit_en is identical to the natural en translation and does not mirror the JP structure, unlike lit_pt which does ('Quanto ao lado do cachorro, em comparação ao gato...'). The field's job is a structural mirror.
findings.current: I like dogs more than cats.
findings.suggested: As for the dog side, compared to the cat, (I) like (it).
